text:
Morgan Geekie scored 39 goals last season, a pace few expected to hold. This season he has five in 22 games on seven expected, and his shooting rate, 14.7%, sits below even our conservative talent range for him. He is getting the looks; they just aren't going in yet.

The points are leaning on the power play: nine of his 17 have come with the man advantage. At five on five the Bruins have taken 51% of the expected goals with him on, a bit worse than when he sits.

The scoring touch came back in a burst (Boston Hockey Now noticed on Nov 11): goals in four straight games from Oct 31 to Nov 8. Then nothing in five, including a Darcy Kuemper stop on a good chance in the 3-0 loss to Los Angeles. His shot is still frightening: 97.8 mph at the top end, 99th percentile on NHL Edge.

What to watch: his ice time has slipped by about a minute and a half over the last ten. Evolving-Hockey had him well ahead of his goals last season on chance quality too, which is a pattern worth trusting more than five quiet nights.
headline: Geekie is getting the chances, not the 39-goal finish
